[{"id": "rjbQEZ-YOF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fCommunications Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "VKtucUkn5K", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Communications module is how the church tells people things. Send a Church Email by email or text message to the whole church or to one group, print and share the weekly bulletin, keep the letters that the church receives, and respect each person's choice about how you may contact them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7t6YLTHX1q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Office users write Church Emails and bulletins. Only a Church Manager (or a System Manager) sends a Church Email. Other staff can read the emails that were sent.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-9GLJSU_ep", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Communications workspace has two shortcuts: Scheduled Emails (the emails that wait to be sent, the soonest first) and Letters To Be Shared. Below them, a chart shows the Church Emails sent each month. The sidebar lists Church Emails, Bulletins, Email Templates, Letters To Be Shared, Communication Consents and, when Raven is installed, Staff Chat. Missionary Letters and Person Letters are in the Letters folder. Bulletin Settings, Communication Purposes, Push Settings and SMS Settings are in the Setup folder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aG0Z8YMDuu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2709\ufe0fChurch Emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zdsHFtcHzi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Church Email sends one message to many people at once, by email or by text message. Each person gets their own copy, so no one sees the other addresses or numbers. Churchit leaves out the people who asked not to get this kind of message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Em6qxYhGX3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Before you can send, a System Manager must set up an outgoing Email Account for emails, or the SMS Settings for texts. Until then, the form says so at the top.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YKC3flykJF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send a Church Email", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5a8190tBEO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Church Emails and click Add Church Email. You can also open a Group and click Actions, then Send Church Email, or tick people in the Person list and click Actions, then New Church Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FzywNe8udG", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. In Send As, choose Email or Text Message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "g8kemuRhYw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. In Purpose, choose what the message is about, such as Church News or Pastoral Care. Only people who allow that purpose get it (see Consent). A new Church Email has Church News. A message started from a Group has Group Messages.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UQ1UyvxuYo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. In Send To, choose who gets it (see below).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GGmICSQuCP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. For an email, write the Subject and the Message. To start from an Email Template, pick it in Template first, then change the text as you like. To send files, save the Church Email and attach them in the sidebar. For a text, write the Text. Up to 160 characters is one text.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HrEIrWI4Hs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Click Actions, then Preview, to see the message as one person gets it, and who does not get a copy and why.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_jQSgobt4u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "7. Click Actions, then Send Test Email or Send Test Text, to get a copy yourself. It goes to the email address of your own user (or your own mobile number).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZP8js1inet", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "8. Click Send. Churchit tells you how many people get it and who is left out, and asks you to confirm.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xvo11WILZQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Office users can do steps 1 to 7. Then a Church Manager opens the email, checks it and clicks Send.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7CU_SAYnrp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The secretary writes the Easter service email to Active Members, previews it and sends a test to herself. She tells the pastor it is ready. The pastor, who is a Church Manager, reads the preview and clicks Send.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4nxc97lw5E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who gets it", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XUkf81AhoF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In Send To, choose:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZZhcv6Qf4m", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Active People: everyone whose Status is Active, whatever their Membership.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "V1XQm8wiYz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Active Members: only the people whose Membership is Member and whose Status is Active.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jJFkLdvybA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Group: the members of one Group, whatever their Status.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CK9CSS3Ie-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Smart List: the people on a saved list of people or a saved Attendance Count (see the People manual). Churchit reads the list when it sends the message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sFj0yYM_Zj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Chosen People: only the people that you put in People.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fOp348d3QC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Include Their Households to also send the message to the people in the Family of each person above. In Household Members, choose Everyone, Adults, or Adults and Other Adults. Each person gets one copy, also when they are in two households.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NWhpHtIFRx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: You send the women's retreat details to the Women's Ministry group and tick Include Their Households with Adults. The husbands get a copy too, but the children do not.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8_y3fynV1q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit works out who gets the message when it sends it, so people who joined or left since you wrote it are counted correctly. It leaves out:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W4c8843oN5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- people who have died,
- people who do not allow the Purpose, or who stopped all emails from the church,
- people with no email address (or no phone number for a text), and addresses marked Bounced,
- for a text, people who have not said yes to texts.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2rpZI62wH9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A household that shares one email address or phone number gets one copy. With more than one church, a Church Email goes only to the people of its own church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lCFg1n_Sxx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Put each person's name in the message", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j8bxq__EqT", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A placeholder puts each person's own name into the message. Write it in double braces, for example \"Dear {{ first_name }},\". You can use {{ first_name }}, {{ last_name }}, {{ display_name }}, {{ full_name }} and {{ church_name }}, in the Subject, the Message and the Text. Churchit refuses any other placeholder and tells you which ones you can use. Preview shows the message with the placeholders filled in for the first person. To see it for someone else, pick them in Person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Akk7cRcvbt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send it later", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W4xdqFhWPy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To send the message later, set Send At before you click Send. It goes out within a few minutes of that time. Until then, a Church Manager can click Actions, then Unschedule, to turn it back into a draft and change it. A scheduled email is locked for Church Office users: ask a Church Manager to unschedule it first. The Scheduled Emails shortcut lists the emails that wait.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-onVE07ZiP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "After it is sent", "col": 12}}, {"id": "YlsW4-8JwO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Number Sent shows how many people it went to, and the Church Email can no longer be changed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fZFfhr9DoI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Each copy shows on the timeline of the person's Person form, as they got it. The Church Email lists its copies in its own timeline.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3kLAaFhdFD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- If sending stops, the Church Email goes back to Draft and a comment on it says why. When you send it again, only the people who did not get it yet get it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zhid9xed8j", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A large message can take a while. If it is still sending after the time allowed, it continues by itself about 15 minutes later.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rxGrk56wbk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text messages", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DEQ56fg28n", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A text goes to each person's primary phone number, and only to people who said yes to texts (see Consent). To send texts, a user must be a System Manager or have a role in the Allowed Roles of the SMS Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "49A_jaJHud", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit checks each text after it sends it. If your text provider (for example, Twilio) refuses a text, Churchit marks that copy Error on the timelines. A copy that left is marked Sent, and Number Sent counts only those. Churchit does not send a refused text again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OD-Xatb4YQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To find the reason, look at the log of your text provider, correct the number on the Person, and send a new message to that person. If the provider refuses every text, for example because of a wrong password, sending stops and the message becomes a draft again. A provider can also accept a text and block it later. Churchit cannot see that, so check the provider's log.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QmhWpjWkCn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Text replies and STOP", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gtiyFmlpXW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit does not receive replies to texts: your text provider gets them. Use a provider that handles STOP replies itself. Twilio does this for numbers in the US and Canada. To change its keywords and reply, put the number in a Twilio Messaging Service, turn on Advanced Opt-Out and send your texts with that Messaging Service.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1NF9Zf4Ppy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In other countries, and with other providers, read the provider's rules. When a person replies STOP, the provider blocks every later text to that number. The person replies START to get texts again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qs0_yptPLP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit does not know about a STOP reply, so it continues to send texts to that number, and each one shows Error. When a person asks to stop texts, record it: add a Communication Consent for the person with the channel SMS and the status Withdrawn.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ouyqE6d2sf", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Leave Purpose blank to stop texts for all purposes. This applies to every text that Churchit sends: Church Emails, group messages, pages to parents at check-in, and serving requests and reminders. A message that also goes by email then reaches the person by email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3Sfsbz4PCE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Mr. Smith replies STOP to a text about the picnic. His provider blocks the next text, and its copy shows Error. The office adds a Withdrawn SMS consent for him, and the next Church Email sent as text leaves him out.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OloksSlDB5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Unsubscribe links", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y9OPADLrT4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every email has an unsubscribe link at the bottom, such as Unsubscribe from Church News emails. The person opens it and clicks Unsubscribe to confirm. They stop getting emails for that purpose only. Group messages, event reminders and pages from the Check-In Station keep coming. A member can change their choices on the Preferences page of the member portal. If a member stopped all emails from the church, the Preferences page says so, and turning on the Church News Email switch starts the emails again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OrzkRkXmYw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Person form of someone who stopped all Church Emails shows Unsubscribed from Church Emails above the tabs. When someone without a portal login asks to get Church Emails again, open their Person and click Actions, then Resubscribe to Church Emails.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "piv3SBVNoa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bounced Emails", "col": 12}}, {"id": "F1WTLK3FBV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When an email cannot reach an address, the mail server sends a report back to the church. This report is a bounce. Churchit reads bounces only when the church's email account also receives mail: open the Email Account that sends the church's email and tick Enable Incoming. Churchit reads the bounces of Gmail, Microsoft 365 and Postfix mail servers. It can miss a bounce from another mail server.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JgFwinNiZF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a bounce says that delivery failed, Churchit ticks Bounced on that address on every record that has it, such as a Person or a Family. It does this only for an address that the church emailed in the last 7 days. A bounce for a full mailbox, a blocked message or a late delivery changes nothing. Church Emails skip a Bounced address, and the Person form shows an orange line: Email bounced.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LYsf-rnQgQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To find bounced addresses, open the People Data Quality report and set Problem to Email Bounced. Ask the person for a new address. When you change the address, Churchit clears Bounced. If you know that the old address works again, untick Bounced on that row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9D8XDODISd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: John's address has a typo, so the next Church Email bounces. Churchit ticks Bounced on his address, and later emails skip him. The office finds him on People Data Quality, calls him and corrects the address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T5UMz4FCv_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who opened an email", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bNzbIwI3QE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When Track Email Status is ticked on the Email Account (it is by default), each copy shows Read on the timelines when the reader's mail app loads it. Many mail apps load nothing until the reader allows images, so fewer copies show Read than people who read the email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GctkKkPE_3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Some mail apps, such as Apple Mail, load every email when it arrives, so a copy can show Read when nobody opened it. To stop this tracking, untick Track Email Status. If you keep it, mention it in the church's privacy notice.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XuU1jFFbas", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email Templates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0bQjMvfQpW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An Email Template is a ready-made Subject and Message. A System Manager adds templates. The Template list on a Church Email shows only the templates that use person placeholders, such as Birthday Greeting, New Member Welcome and Visitor Follow-Up. The other templates belong to features such as sign-ups, ministry teams and giving, which fill in their own placeholders. Do not use them for Church Emails, and change their placeholders with care.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XNtFVtYAh3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Email from the Person list", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AlSW_8cnPN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Person list also has Email and Email Household Adults in its actions. These open your own mail app with the people in BCC. They do not check consent, add no unsubscribe link and keep no copy on the Person. For church news, use a Church Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w1cqMLMyFg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Draft with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Oxqc96meiB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), some text fields have a Draft with AI link beside their label. The AI writes, shortens, changes the tone of or translates the text of that field:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "12t3ustwV_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Email: Subject, Message and Text.
- Bulletin: Welcome Message and Announcements.
- Email Template: Subject and Response.
- Function, Group and Sermon Series: Description.
- Follow-up Workflow: the Text Message of a row in Actions.
- Web Page: Description in Meta Tags, and the alt text of pictures (see the Website manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4Iu_DEj8kA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Click Draft with AI beside the field.
2. In Action, choose Write, Shorten, Change Tone or Translate. In Request, say what you want, for example \"warmer\" for Change Tone or \"Spanish\" for Translate.
3. Click Draft and read the suggestion.
4. Click Use to put it in the field, or close the window to keep your text.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gK5QlMPsOz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use changes only the form. Nothing is saved or sent until you save, and a Church Email goes out only when you click Send. A person can use Draft with AI 20 times an hour.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "jzQaBJjEBz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The AI gets your request, the text in the field, the name of your church and a few facts about the record, such as the name, date and place of a Function. It never gets a person, a prayer request or a gift.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "USlhmXSQ7z", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "For a saved Function that is not published, the AI model needs a Privacy Label of No training or better (see the Foundations manual). An answer for a Church Email can use only the name placeholders. If an answer leaves out a placeholder that your text had, the window says so: put it back before you save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vMuuUq4Npl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The AI must not quote a Bible verse. It names a passage, and Churchit checks it: a sentence that names a passage that is not in the Bible is left out, and the window says so. Under Bible passages, the window shows the words from your church's default free translation. Check each passage in your Bible.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HOMwHGCPOt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf0Bulletins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GIjfmzI8Ju", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Bulletin is the printed handout for one service or event (a Function): a Letter sheet printed on both sides and folded in half. The front cover has the church name, the function name and date, a cover image and the verse of the week. The inside and the back hold the sections that you switch on. Members can also read it in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZWaom20YB8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Office users make and edit bulletins. Church Managers set the default sections in Bulletin Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BY4DY5CYAV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make a bulletin", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fch9VMkP-L", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open the Function and click Actions, then New Bulletin. Or open Bulletins, click Add Bulletin and pick the Function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5BbbqPKN9I", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Check what Churchit filled in (see below).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HF432jtPGN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Attach a cover image, type the verse of the week, such as John 3:16, and write the welcome message and the announcements. Click Copy from last week to start from your last bulletin's welcome and announcements.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Bu3xVqUhCv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. Under Sections at the end of the form, switch off any section that you do not want in this bulletin.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZxKviBB1yo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6IXnO75ov3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A new bulletin starts with:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PYHl_JSi2J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- the sections that are on in Bulletin Settings,", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A9LRUr2EPR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- the Missionary of the Week, picked in turn from your current missionaries (see the Missions manual). Change it if you like.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PlDMot01wS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- the open prayer requests that are shared with the Whole Church and approved for the list, urgent first (see the Prayers manual). Remove the rows that you do not want printed. Other requests cannot be added.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Mj_SeyCWaO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If you change the Function of a bulletin later, Churchit picks the Missionary of the Week and the prayer requests again, and your changes to those rows are lost.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zSPC1TuIXm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the automatic sections print", "col": 12}}, {"id": "toW5G9reAr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Order of Worship: the function's schedule, with times and the titles of linked songs, sermons and other items. When no item has a time, the time column is left out. A Collection item prints as Offering.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gqZgbgqrWO", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Leadership: the people who hold the church roles chosen in Bulletin Settings, such as Pastor or Elder, on the function date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PmXaJdKEBw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Upcoming Functions: the functions in the days after the function date (Bulletin Settings sets how many days). It lists every function in those days, also functions that are not published, so check it before you print.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gQSzVb4li7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Ministries: the active ministries and their mission statements.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_SIK66NPcA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Birthdays and Anniversaries: from the function date, for the number of days in Bulletin Settings, for active members or everyone. Only names and days print, no ages or years. People with Hide from Directory and Bulletin ticked, and people who have died, are left out, and so is a couple's anniversary when either spouse is.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mXXtCAxpCC", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Prayer Requests: the title of each request and the name of the person it is for, never the request text.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O3uQueVpt2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Missionary of the Week: the photo, country, agency and Mission Statement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "BxIUOP7sPD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Verse: the verse of the Church record, at the foot of the back cover.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6hQJ8ydcSl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church Image: the image of the Church, such as a logo, above the church name on the front cover.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qFvyK-5E2w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Contact Information: the address, phone, email and website of the Church. A branch with no website prints its parent church's website. A missing phone or email comes from Contact Us Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y4UhZ6dcMr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Sermon Handout Insert: when a sermon on the schedule has a Sermon Handout, a third sheet prints it twice, to cut into two half-page inserts (see the Study manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T5y2UXc7Pu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Verses print with their words in your church's Default Bible Translation once that translation has its text, and as the reference alone until then. A section with nothing to print is left out.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hlSdhpEclJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Print it", "col": 12}}, {"id": "esfKWJuQcP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Print Bulletin. The bulletin opens in a new tab with the print window of your browser. To keep a PDF, choose Save as PDF there. Print it double-sided on Letter paper, flipped on the short edge, and fold it in half. Each panel has a fixed space, so shorten a section or switch one off if text is cut off. For the handout sheet, print half as many copies and cut them on the dashed line.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "5hFoY6_ZuM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Share it online", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d2qVc80O74", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Show in Portal to share the bulletin with your members. Members who sign in see it on the Bulletins page of the member portal, and the newest one shows on their home page. They can read it in the browser or download the PDF. A member sees only the bulletins of their own church. A visitor who opens a bulletin link goes to the login page first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QUYZ3XGGzS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Public announcements. To show the announcements to everyone, tick Show in Portal and Show Announcements on the Website. The public Announcements page shows the announcements of the five newest bulletins with both boxes ticked, and the member portal's home page shows the newest ones. Nothing else of the bulletin is public: no welcome, no prayer requests, no birthdays and no order of worship. To add Announcements to the website menu, see the Website manual.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eGzdOzzfT6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Images. Each image that you add to a bulletin's text is a public file, so anyone with its link can open it. The church image on the cover shows to members only when it is a public file. When staff print, it always shows. To make it public, open the File list, open the image, clear Is Private and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DeUDPv4nAJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Each Thursday the secretary makes Sunday's bulletin from the Function, copies last week's welcome and edits it, adds the announcements and prints 150 copies. She ticks Show in Portal so members can read it at home, and Show Announcements on the Website so that visitors see the coming events.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "m1k-lUVngo", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JTaKRWe3fn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give a church its own set of sections, add a row for it under Sections Per Church in Bulletin Settings. A row replaces the whole set for that church, so tick every section that it wants. Click a row to see its switches. The Church Roles list is shared by all churches, but each church's bulletin names its own people in those roles.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RDGT3_akul", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcddLetters", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2_i1ch8TMi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churches receive letters: prayer letters from missionaries, thank-you notes, letters from members. Keep each letter on the Person or Missionary who sent it, in the Letters to the Church table. Then you have a history, and you know which letters the church has heard.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "h9sIFfMPVM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open the Person or the Missionary and add a row to Letters to the Church. The row starts with today's date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NMYWbA8dAL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. Attach the letter in File, or click the pencil icon at the end of the row and type the text in Content.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3QEz-CPwem", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. Tick Share With Church when someone should read the letter to the church. Tick Private for a letter that the church must not hear: it hides Share With Church and Shared Date and keeps the letter off the reports. Private does not hide the letter from staff who can open the record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qDav2XwXGm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. After the letter is read to the church, open the row and fill in the Shared Date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3SR-lKIKvR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Share With Church publishes nothing. No web page shows letters. The box only puts the letter on the Letters To Be Shared report (in the sidebar and on the workspace), which lists the letters with Share With Church ticked and no Shared Date. When you fill in the Shared Date, the letter leaves the report. Private letters are never on it. Missionary Letters and Person Letters (in the Letters folder) list all letters.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "LqoI86ZHVD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Missionary Mike sends a prayer letter by email. The secretary attaches it on his Missionary record and ticks Share With Church. On Saturday the pastor opens Letters To Be Shared, sees Mike's letter and reads it in the service. On Monday the secretary fills in the Shared Date, and the letter leaves the list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HQU2ZkbN8-", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u2705Consent", "col": 12}}, {"id": "W2z4gCECiP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People can choose how the church may contact them. A Communication Consent records one answer: the person, the channel (email, text message, push notification, phone or post), a purpose (or blank for every purpose), Given or Withdrawn, when they said it and how. A person's consents are on the Connections tab of their Person form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kxsFJguRkS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Mrs. Lee no longer wants the church newsletter, but she wants to hear from the care team. She has a Withdrawn consent for email with the purpose Church News. A Church News email leaves her out. An email with the purpose Pastoral Care still reaches her.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pIghHLvIEJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Record an answer", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WkdxEo8mgc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church People Editor, Church Pastoral Care and Church Manager users can add a consent. The answer cannot be changed after you save it. If someone changes their mind, click Record a Change of Mind and save the new answer. The newest answer counts. When two answers have the same date and time, the one saved last counts. A yes for every purpose does not undo a no for one purpose: to start that purpose again, record a yes for that purpose.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AEoPhTppBJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Purposes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2IoAtzmeUm", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Communication Purpose is a reason the church contacts people, such as Church News or Pastoral Care. Churchit uses some of them itself, so you cannot delete them:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hmEM2fFHvM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Church News: a new Church Email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2dQ62ndb-b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Group Messages: a Church Email sent from a Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WURtkLnUpB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Child Safety: a page to parents from the Check-In Station.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eaWyjVsKCx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Event Registrations: reminders of a function sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JSSnw1ahN0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Serving: ministry team requests and reminders. A person gets a ministry team text only with text consent for Serving, but the ministry team emails go to everyone asked to serve.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "vnFE4D-TJD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can add your own purposes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sNfOiu4MWq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ask first, or contact until they say no", "col": 12}}, {"id": "65kkSEMMfw", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the UK, the EU and other places, the law says that people must agree before a church contacts them. In that case, tick Contact People Only With Their Consent on the Settings tab of the Church. The church then contacts only people who said yes. When the box is not ticked, the church contacts people until they say no. The church never contacts a person who has died.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2NEY0j-x4v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Texts and push notifications always need a yes first, also when the box is not ticked. A person can say yes on the Preferences page of the member portal, on a Connection Card, or to you. To record a yes that a person tells you, add a Communication Consent with the channel SMS (or Push).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "C7AbX1DF42", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where answers come from", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gqm91koae4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Unsubscribe links: when someone unsubscribes from a Church News email, or turns off Church News email on the Preferences page, everyone at your church who uses that email address is recorded as having said no to Church News. The link in an email with another purpose records a no to that purpose only. A resubscribe from the Person form records a yes for that person only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O3g2sY6iLk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Preferences page: signed-in members see their primary email address and phone number, and one row for each purpose with an Email switch. A Text switch shows when texts are set up and the member has a phone number. A Push switch shows when the member allowed notifications on a device. A switch saves at once. A member with no email address sees a note to contact the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PqYjQ8sUqQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Connection Cards: the Stay in Touch section has Email Me Church News and Events and Text Me Church News and Events. When Churchit processes the card, each ticked box records a yes to Church News. It records nothing when the card has no email or phone for it, when the card is Spam, or when the card is linked to a person who does not have that email or phone yet. A ticked box does not replace an earlier no.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SfTA9OgnkN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Automatic emails (Notifications) leave out an address only when no person who uses it may be contacted. Staff always get the work notices meant for them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QJYyO2hyip", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ask people to renew their consent", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Y6JR9YH33t", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A church that ticks Contact People Only With Their Consent can ask people every two years whether they still want its emails. A System Manager duplicates the Consent Renewal notification and turns the copy on (see Shipped notifications below). Two years after a person last said yes to email, the copy emails them a Yes, keep in touch link. The person needs no login.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Tu-6fr-3tB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The link records a new yes for each email purpose that the person allows, and the next reminder comes two years later. If the person does nothing, Churchit does not ask again until they next change their choices. To ask after a different time, change Days Before or After on your copy. People who said no last, and people who have died, get no reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "So8lO-Gipv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd14Notifications", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sOa_iVKJ52", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Notification is an automatic email that Churchit sends when something happens, such as a new prayer request or a task that is due. The people it is for also see it in the bell at the top of the desk. When the site has no Email Account that can send, the email is not sent, but the bell still shows it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FJB8hfrdkR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These notifications are on when Churchit is installed. A System Manager can change who gets them and what they say in Notifications (in the Settings sidebar):", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZcWjc5U4Hv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- New Prayer Request for the Prayer Team, Approved Prayer Request for the Prayer Team and New Private Prayer Request (see the Prayers manual).
- New Care Request, New Alms Request and Alms Request Approved (see the People and Finances manuals).
- Church Task Due and Room Booking Decided (see the Operations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "P3Gafo0EAx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The reminders for overdue follow-up cards, overdue care requests and planned visits are turned on and off in People Settings, under Reminders. A System Manager can change their text in Notifications, but not turn them on or off there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X2QrheCSOu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Shipped notifications", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0ckYEiWtAS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit also ships notifications that are off until a System Manager turns them on:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eM7W876_4O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Birthday Greeting: emails an active person on their birthday.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gaa_1rsmR8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Anniversary Greeting: emails the primary contact of a married, active couple on their anniversary.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fj0rZceBwJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- New Member Welcome: emails a person when their Membership becomes Member and their Status is Active, with a link to the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nwtTPAORRr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Visitor Follow-Up: emails the Church Managers when someone is added as a Visitor (or with no Membership).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Do6IWpD5IV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Function Reminder 24h: emails every user with the Church User role, which is every member with a portal login, the day before each published function that does not repeat. Turn it on only if you want all members to get these reminders.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "f0mdrNW50c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Meeting Minutes Published: emails the minutes to the Church Managers when they are published.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a2anXAKzkg", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Position Term Ending: emails the Church Managers 30 days before a position ends.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "m0R6QKbRwX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Background Check Expiring: emails the Church Pastoral Care users 30 days before a background check expires.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H8rtn9LHv2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Expense Pending Approval: emails the Church Managers about a new expense.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "d1HwWxydu0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Consent Renewal: see Consent above.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CbWd6fvdWX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A shipped notification cannot be turned on itself. To use one:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "y6tUvJc02D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Notifications (in the Settings sidebar) and open the notification by its name.
2. Click the ... menu, then Duplicate.
3. Tick Enabled on the copy and save it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "G7anBBiDvq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Your copy keeps its text when Churchit is updated. To get a newer text, duplicate the shipped notification again. A receipt for each giver of a collection is a setting in Giving Settings (see the Finances manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rdmrQMvPrp", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udda5\ufe0fPresentations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "DAzMd-VW-D", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit shows the slides of a Sermon full screen in the browser: open the sermon and click Present. The Study manual explains how to build the slides, and what visitors see on a published sermon. Slide notes show on the screen, so do not write private notes there. To present songs, or for more complex services, we recommend FreeShow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mw7oB_-nsP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf1Notifications on Phones", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Gw_sT67oR9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit can show notifications on a member's phone or computer, through the installed app or the browser. No extra service is needed. No feature sends push notifications yet. When one does, only members who allowed notifications on a device, and turned on Push for that purpose, will get them. Everyone else gets the message by email or text, when the feature sends those.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qVqWPmCsB1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Set it up. A System Manager opens Push Settings, types the Contact Address as mailto: and the church office email, for example mailto:office@example.org, and saves. Then click Generate Keys once, tick Enabled and save. Do not remove the keys later, because each device that allowed notifications uses them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9nhE2DD1B2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Allow notifications on a device. A member opens the Preferences page of the member portal and clicks Allow notifications, then allows them in the browser. They do this on each phone or computer. On an iPhone or iPad, the member must first add the site to the Home Screen and open it from there (iOS 16.4 or later).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "K7p4CQGo51", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A member who allows notifications on a shared device takes that device over from the person before them. After that, the page shows a Push switch for each purpose, off until the member turns it on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bdMo0ecuBB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcacStaff Chat", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PoiZ9DY82G", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit has no chat of its own. For chat between staff, a System Manager can install Raven, a free Frappe app, on the same site. The Communications sidebar then has a Staff Chat link. Only a person with the Raven User role can use Raven. Members cannot: to message a group, a leader uses Message the group in the member portal.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3LNMi_EGys", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Raven does not follow Churchit's church rules. Each Raven user sees the name, photo and phone number of all other Raven users, and a person in a Raven channel sees all of its messages, also from the staff of another church. So give Raven only to staff who may see the staff of all churches:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "R7VadzNBEE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Right after you install Raven, open Raven Settings and turn off Automatically add system users to Raven.
2. Give the Raven User role by hand to each person who may use Raven. To stop a person, remove the role.
3. Make one Raven workspace for each church, with Type Private and Can only join via invite? ticked, and add the staff of that church to it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cAewUuXzVI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Private records. A Raven Document Notification copies the text of a record into a chat message that everyone in the channel can read, also people who cannot open the record. Do not set a Document Notification on Person, Person Note, Care Request, Counseling Case, Prayer Request or Background Check. Keep Raven AI off: other AI bots can answer in a channel, and every member of the channel, from every church, reads the answer.", "col": 12}}]
